Counts are distinct findings on each outer artifact. Every analyzed archive member also has zero hostile and suspicious findings before and after. All classifiers remain benign (`level: -1`); no judgement/classifier disagreement or material attack-detection loss remains. `comparison.json` records member counts and every added/removed ID, including two descriptive renames.

The baseline and final scans used the working checkout explicitly, local slow analysis, and `--follow=none`. Initial exploratory scans used `--follow none`, which the CLI interpreted as an extra nonexistent path; those are not the comparison baseline. Raw baseline/final scans, facts (including decoded layers), member facts and consumer inventories are under `/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-90084b2c/scratch/bad-batch/`; the initial facts dump is under `scratch/review/facts.jsonl`. Scores supplied leads, not verdict evidence.

The extension's manifest overrides newtab.html and loads js/background.js as its service worker. It grants search, alarms, storage and api.gameograf.com access, with no content-script, all-site, cookies, history or scripting grant. The onInstalled callback checks `reason === "install"` before opening one publisher landing tab, fetching message/shortcut JSON and registering a 30-minute alarm. Startup and that alarm refresh those JSON records into chrome.storage.local. An uninstall URL opens a publisher page. These are visible promotion and lifecycle functions, not evidence of ongoing coerced advertising impressions.

script.js reads the shortcut records from storage, reacts to storage changes, filters navigation schemes to HTTP(S), permits deletion/reordering and inserts shortcut markup with jQuery. Its URL, name and icon fields are not HTML-escaped; the scheme check does not prevent attribute or element injection through those fields. This is a real rendering weakness. The artifact and recovered feed do not contain a malicious breakout payload. popup.js ignores the feed's legacy `html` field and builds its banner with textContent and createElement; it assigns a button href, supports dismissal and an off toggle. Search runs after a user click/Enter and uses chrome.search.query with the configured provider. Other scripts implement local notes, todos, calculator arithmetic, a calendar, clock, timers, an audio oscillator beep, manual weather-city settings and external app links. Weather requests send the configured city or use server-side IP geolocation. No host credential survey, external-page injection, IndexedDB deletion, hidden advertising frame, forced search query, downloaded executable stage or obfuscated first-party payload was found in the traced entry points.

All JavaScript was read; jQuery's minification was compared with the official 3.7.1 minified distribution. Both hashes are `fc9a93dd241f6b045cbff0481cf4e1901becd0e12fb45166a8f17f95823f0b1a`. Its dynamic script helpers are ordinary upstream library capabilities, not a publisher payload. The icons identify as PNG and the wallpaper as MP4. The integrity JSON's Base64 payload decodes to treehash/file-hash metadata, not a second executable stage. Its signature records are asserted metadata; no cryptographic verification or trust inference is claimed.

Forager recovered the referenced message.json, shortcuts.json, privacy policy, installation landing page and official jQuery. The current shortcut feed has six links (wallpapers, Amazon, YouTube, Netflix, styles, games), ordinary icon URLs and no executable markup. The message promotes another extension with plain-text fields and a click-through URL; its legacy HTML is unused by this build. The landing page is a publisher WordPress page with advertising/analytics, and the policy discloses advertising and IP/content-server use. Weather returned HTTP 204 to this requester; no weather body was available. These observations do not prove what historical or future responses contain. Consent history and deployment policy are unavailable.

[Unit42's campaign note](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/refs/heads/main/2026-06-01-Adware-Wallpaper-Chrome-Extension-Campaign.txt) describes Gameograf and related publishers, coerced ad traffic, destructive IndexedDB operations and HTML injection. Publisher association and earlier/related builds plausibly explain the queue label; this is an inference, not proof of an earlier version's behavior. This September-era build does retain unsafe shortcut templating, but its observed code and fetched data do not establish the hostile campaign actions. Ordinary visible, user-removable promotion plus that weakness does not tip these particular bytes to malicious.

Endurance.csproj.user is a complete 482-byte UTF-8/BOM XML document in the MSBuild schema. Parsing the entire tree yields Project, PropertyGroup, relative `PublishUrlHistory` (`publish\`), empty install/support/update/bootstrapper/error-report histories, `FallbackCulture=en-US`, and `VerifyUploadedFiles=false`. There are no Target, Task, UsingTask, Import, commands, event hooks, URLs to fetch, encoded stages or referenced executable dependencies. The upload-verification preference is not evidence of disabling signature verification or running a build action. The existing MSBuild-root observation is accurate and sufficient for this inert settings document. The containing project and source provenance were not supplied; incidental collection from a flagged project is a possible explanation, not an assumed deployment circumstance.

cacheable-request 5.2.1 contains package.json, LICENSE, README.md and src/index.js. The recovered npm tarball's SHA-256 exactly equals the submitted `16e19a8ba5e223a66dff39bfc8cceddfef16529f64307976d26d96c111262dc5`. The manifest has test/coverage scripts, no install lifecycle hook, and main=src/index.js. Importing it defines/exports the wrapper and errors; it does not send a request until a caller constructs and invokes it. The constructor validates a caller-supplied request function and initializes Keyv. Its returned wrapper normalizes the caller's URL/options, keys a cache by method and URL, returns fresh cached response streams, adds conditional revalidation headers for stale entries, invokes the supplied request function on a miss, clones responses, buffers storable bodies, writes cache policy/body/status/URL with TTL, and deletes stale non-storable entries. Error handling supports an explicit automatic-failover option. This is the advertised RFC HTTP caching purpose, with no execution, secret collection, hidden endpoint or obfuscated loader.

Forager recovered and the source was inspected for the resolved direct runtime dependencies: clone-response 1.0.3, get-stream 4.1.0, http-cache-semantics 4.3.0, keyv 3.1.0, lowercase-keys 1.0.1, normalize-url 3.3.0 and responselike 1.0.2. They implement stream cloning/buffering, cache header policy, Keyv storage, header casing, URL normalization and readable response objects. Keyv's optional adapter require is selected by caller configuration; its default store is Map. The unusual `this` 1.0.2 development dependency was also fetched/read: it loads the root package for tests via pkg-dir, not a hidden install hook. The sample has no lockfile, so an actual machine's resolved dependency tree cannot be reconstructed from this artifact alone. Optional adapter packages and all development dependency trees were not represented as part of these supplied bytes.

The cited [Aikido overview](https://www.aikido.dev/blog/dark-figure-supply-chain-detection) links the [Keyv compromise report](https://www.aikido.dev/blog/keyv-and-friends-compromised-in-npm-supply-chain-attack), which identifies cacheable-request **13.0.20** and keyv **6.0.0**, with a concealed preinstall/Bun/payload chain. Those are different versions from this sample and its declared Keyv ^3.0.0 range. The clean upstream-equivalent old tarball and traced implementation support a version-insensitive feed association as the likely mislabel explanation.

The rule changes add five notable observations: browser storage entry deletion, extension storage-change listener registration, Web Audio oscillator construction, conditional cache revalidation headers and cached-response header generation. Matchers use parsed call sites, so comments, string mentions, method definitions and unattached member references do not satisfy them. Network behavior remains notable. Two extension composites are renamed/reworded without matcher or scope changes to describe lifecycle/fetch and newtab/catalog/store co-occurrence without inventing data flow.

The package-name matcher moves from well-known library identity to metadata/package/name/identity with the same value, scope, confidence and criticality. The pure name/path OR composite's library-implementation claim was unsupported: a tiny package.json can claim that name without implementing it. The preexisting vendored-path atom is unchanged, preserving its out-of-batch match scope. No generic library suppressor receives a new source-code fingerprint.

The old verified-contents finding only tested an archive member name, despite claiming signed contents and being filed as a permission. The replacement in metadata/signed/platform reads the actual nested JWS `header.kid=webstore` value and describes an asserted header, not signature validity. A named empty file demonstrates the unsupported old claim; a renamed JSON member demonstrates the corrected property. The existing permission-profile downgrade retains its old member-name predicate inline, rather than treating the new signature-header finding as a broader trust suppressor. Explicit references and ancestor selectors were inspected; broad signed suppressors have no archive-scoped downgrade that gains this JSON finding.

Ten static controls pass. They cover positive calls, comment/string/declaration near misses, claimed package identity, empty integrity filenames, asserted signature headers, renamed signature members and existing out-of-batch hostile relay/XSS fixtures. Comparing controls with original HEAD rules shows identical hostile/suspicious IDs and criticalities; the earlier experimental header-based downgrade was rejected because it lost hostile coverage on a renamed unverified-header control. It is not in the final rules. No shared hostile matcher was weakened and no accurate behavior was removed to lower a score. Run `python3 testdata/triage/batch-55b1fe-169b4f-16e19a/check.py` for the controls. Final repository check: `make validate`.

`markers.json` preserves the exact one-line contents of the three adjacent `.BENIGN` markers. `fetched.json` locates every recovered artifact and its retained `.forage.json` provenance. No sample or recovered script was executed.
